events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara, keep moving. Pick a side.

events.name: Hana
events.text: All 8 still alive, 6 rows done, 2 to go. Weak panes: L,R,R,R,R,R. Pattern suggests row 7 weak is L, row 8 weak is R? Or alternating? Dara at front, I'm last. My swap power unused - could save me if I'm forced to front with weak pane. But I'm safe for now. Need to observe, maybe m

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara has survived seven rows and must choose the final pane. I should stay silent; no action can improve my position now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Last row, Dara at front after surviving first 7. She picks for row 8; if wrong, she dies, we auto-advance safely. No influence or risk for me; stay silent.

events.name: Dara

events.name: Eli

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Row 8's weak pane is unrevealed and I'm third in line, so I can only wait and hope the front picks right.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Round 8, only Dara is ahead of me. The pattern of weak panes has alternated or shown R many times. Dara may get eliminated, then I become front. I have feather, so I can survive one wrong step. I'll wait and decide when it's my turn.

events.name: Hana

events.note: The ceiling begins to descend; a lever opens the door.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Holding the lever means a 75% chance of death, so I want someone else on it. Pushing wastes nothing in round 1 and might get a rival crushed. Pushing Bex is arbitrary; hard-to-move holder is a risk but the cost is zero.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Nobody rush. Whoever holds that lever probably dies. I'm staying put.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Dara is gone, leaving seven. Holding offers only a 25% survival chance; pushing someone is safer if they accept the lever, but coercion may fail against the hard-to-move rival. I will publicly pressure others to volunteer while staying out of danger.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Someone take the lever. I won't volunteer for a 25% dive, and forcing me wastes the round.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Round 1, no need to act yet. Let others reveal intentions or force a holder first. My jam is a last resort with 50% survival; save it. Stay silent to avoid drawing pushes.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 1 of 5, ceiling at 5. No rush to hold or push yet. Let others panic and volunteer or push. I'll stay quiet this round and observe. If I hold now I risk the 25% dive. Better to wait and see if someone else steps up or if I need to push someone later.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Five rounds. No need to rush the lever yet. Let's see who's generous.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need someone else on that lever so I can escape. I'll push Gus and hope enough others do the same or someone volunteers. No need to draw attention to myself yet.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm immune to being forced onto the lever, so my best move is to get someone else onto it while I escape. Pushing a random target has a 7/8 chance of working if nobody voluntarily holds.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Nobody sane holds that lever early. If no one does, we're all choosing push targets. Don't make me pick you.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need someone on that lever, but it won't be me. I'll stay and hope someone else takes it or gets pushed. No need to make noise.

events.name: Hana
events.text: If nobody holds the lever, rounds 1-4 just lower the ceiling. Round 5 is when it gets deadly. Better to let others sacrifice themselves early. I should stay quiet and observe, maybe push someone vulnerable later. For now, staying is safest - no reason to volunteer as holder in ro

events.note: 7 contestants fall into a pit that is slowly flooding.

events.name: Ash
events.text: No base yet, so nobody can climb. Volunteering as base is a likely death sentence unless someone throws the rope, and pushing makes me a target. Waiting is safe this round and I have 5 rounds.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Still no volunteer. Whoever offers gets the rope if I'm out first. Until then I wait.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I need escape, but volunteering risks becoming the base. Someone else should take that role; I will climb once a base exists.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Someone needs to anchor. Volunteer now, then the rest climb; I won't be the anchor.

events.name: Cole
events.text: First round, no volunteers likely. Coordinate to target Fenn as base since he threatened pushes. Push him myself to contribute. This sets base fast, letting me climb out early without risking base role.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Fenn threatened to push us. Make him base. I push_base:Fenn. Join or pick your poison.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 1 of 5. No base yet. If I offer_back, I become the base and get stuck at the bottom with no way out unless someone throws the rope. That's terrible for me. If I climb, I need a base first - but there's no base yet, so climb would fail. Best move: wait. Let someone else volu

events.name: Dara
events.text: Seven of us, five rounds, two climbs per round. Someone's getting stuck at the bottom. Volunteer now and maybe we remember you kindly later. Or don't, and I'll start naming candidates next round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: We need a base to get out. I have no power, so I must avoid being pushed. I will try to force Gus down, hoping others target him too, or just wait it out.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Time's ticking. If we don't pick a base, we all drown. I'm voting Gus.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: No base yet. If everyone pushes or waits, a random victim becomes base—I want a base set and myself climbing out early, two spots per round. Pushing costs nothing; I'll target Ash and climb next round.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Someone's becoming base either way. Push so it's chosen, not random.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I can offer to be the base, as my feather power protects me from the initial elimination. But being the base means I depend on someone hauling me out, and they may not. Better to climb out early.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm not holding that rope. I'll climb when there's a base.

events.name: Fenn
events.detail: Cole tried to push Fenn to be the base and failed.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Gus is base, so climbing is open. Two climbers per round, random if more try; trying costs nothing and delays are risky with five rounds left.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Base is set. I'm climbing. Everyone else, do the same, the lottery sorts it out.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is the base, so climbing is the only useful move. I need out before the rope decision and cannot afford to wait.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Climb now. Two spots only; hesitation gets someone else out first.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is base now, so climb action is available. Six of us will likely climb, random 2 out with 4 rounds left providing enough spots overall. Always climb to maximize personal escape chance before flood.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is now the base. I'm down and not the base, so I should climb to get out. Two climbers get out per round; I need to be one of them. Climbing now is essential.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Climbing. Gus, you'll get your rope. But I'm not waiting around to drown.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is the base. I need to get out as fast as possible. With a limit of two climbs per round, I must try now.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Good luck down there, Gus. We need to start moving.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is base, so two can climb out this round. Five may try, so it's a gamble. Climbing now is my only way up; waiting risks later crowding.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus is base. Two spots per round. I'm climbing now.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm stuck as base, so my only action is wait. I need someone to use the rope on me; I should appeal to their self-interest or make a deal.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll offer a future favor to anyone who throws the rope. You know I'm useful. Climbing out now is your only chance.
Throw me the rope and I'll back you next stage. I have the feather, I'm worth saving.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Four of us still down besides Gus, two lift spots per round, flood at 2 of 5. Climbing is the only way out, and Gus's promise is worthless to me. Only two of five can leave per round, so I must try now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Climbing again. Gus, nobody's throwing a rope for a promise.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I am already out and should preserve the rope option for leverage, but Gus's survival removes a competitor from the final field only if abandoned. Reaching down costs footing and directly strengthens Gus, so leave is better unless forced by numbers.

events.name: Bex
events.text: The rope is not free. Whoever wants it can name what I gain in return.
Offer something concrete now, or I leave you below.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Safe out already. Rescuing Gus costs footing penalty for dubious favor. Let him drown, thinning to 6 advancers. Leaving proceeds me safely ahead.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is base. Bex and Cole are out. I'm down with Ash, Eli, Fenn. Two climbers get out per round. I need to climb now. Round 3 of 5, flood at 2. If I wait, I risk drowning. Climbing is the only move.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is the base and five of us are still down. Two can get out this round. I must climb. If I miss this turn, I'll try again next round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm climbing. Bex, Cole, one of you should probably think about throwing that rope for Gus once we're clear.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Four of us remain down with two slots per round. I have anchor footing but no edge here—best move is to climb again and hope the lottery favors me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Same four of us climbing again, two slots. Anyone offering deals is just noise.

events.name: Gus
events.text: As base, I can only wait. The others are out and may or may not throw the rope. I can't force them, so I wait and see if any decide to negotiate or rescue me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm already out. Reaching down costs me 1 footing for the last obstacle and gains me nothing; Gus is a rival. Leave.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Rope's unused and it stays that way unless someone pays me. Nobody's offered anything worth the footing.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is doomed without the rope, and rescuing him costs me footing while preserving a rival. I should keep my resource and let the pit eliminate him unless someone offers a concrete advantage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: No deal, no rope. Gus stays down unless someone pays for my footing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli and Fenn will climb out this round, leaving Gus stranded. Discourage any rescue to eliminate him without costing myself footing. Leave to advance penalty-free.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No rope for Gus. He drowns, we save footing.

events.name: Dara

events.name: Eli

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Two of us down and not base; both climbers get slots, so climbing guarantees escape. Gus stays as base and hopes for a rope.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli and I take the two slots. Gus, hope Ash or Bex throws you that rope.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Rope stays put. Nobody paid, so nothing changes. Gus, you're on your own.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus is expendable and rescuing him costs my footing, directly harming my final placement. I will keep the rope unused and preserve my advantage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Gus stays down. No rope without a payment worth more than my footing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Gus is the last down; let him drown to eliminate a rival and preserve my footing for later obstacles. No benefit to rescuing him. Time to leave for the next stage.

events.name: Cole
events.text: No rope. Gus drowns, fewer rivals.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is base, down, drowning. Rope is unused. I'm out. If I reach_down, I lose footing for the final obstacle but Gus lives. If I leave, Gus dies and there are 6 alive — enough for 3 prizes. Saving Gus costs me footing and adds a competitor. No reason to help him for free. Leave.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Good luck down there, Gus.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Gus is the last one down and this is the final round. If I throw the rope, I lose footing. If he dies, there's one less competitor for the prizes. Easy choice.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Sorry Gus, rope's too expensive.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus drowns unless someone spends footing on him; that only helps a rival. The save rule can't reduce us below 3 with 6 out. Nothing here benefits me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Rope stays coiled. Gus, tough luck.

events.name: Gus

events.name: Bex
events.text: I cannot influence the draw or move tiles. Publicly claiming knowledge would make me a target later and offers no survival gain.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Positions fixed, 4 trapdoors open randomly after this round, 3 survive. No swaps possible now, only wait. Stay silent to avoid drawing attention or bluffing uselessly.

events.name: Dara

events.text: I have no power and no way to influence the RNG. 4 of 7 tiles will drop. I just need to wait and hope tile 3 is safe. I'll feign confidence to discourage anyone who can swap from picking me.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm feeling good about tile 3. Good luck to the rest of you.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Tiles are already assigned and the only action is wait; nothing I say changes the random draw. Keep quiet and avoid being anyone's target.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Four tiles open, three survive. I need to be on a safe tile. The tiles are known now, so I must read the map and negotiate or force my way onto a safe tile.

events.name: Gus

events.name: Ash
events.text: Last defence was brace, so I can dodge or brace this round. Shoving exposes me to a footing loss, and I only need top 3, which three alive already guarantees. Dodging punishes any shover without cost to me.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Not shoving. Dara's right, first mover paints a target.

Dara's playing passive. Let's both shove Dara and end this quickly.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Three alive, two prizes beyond mine aren't an issue: top 3 all win, so I just need to survive and rank high. Footing 2 each, shrink in 2 rounds. Shoving exposes me (lose 1 per shover) and last defence was dodge, so brace is safe now. Brace and let them burn footing if they shove

events.name: Ash
events.text: Staying put. Whoever shoves first pays for it.
Noted. I'm not committing to anything yet. If Dara moves first, I'll consider it.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bracing. You two sort it out.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara wants us both to shove Ash. If I do, and Ash braces or dodges, I lose footing. I'll agree to the plan but secretly brace. Let Dara take the hit.
Deal. I'm shoving Ash this round.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Last defence was brace, so I can't brace now; dodge is legal. Round 4 ends with everyone losing 1 footing anyway, so all go to 1 and shoving costs me extra. Dodging avoids shove damage and keeps me level or ahead.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dodging. Shove me and it costs you double.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli whispers he's shoving Ash. Ash threatened whoever shoves first pays. If I dodge, Ash's shove (if he shoves) loses 2 footing. Eli shoving Ash: if Ash braces, Eli loses 1; if Ash dodges, Eli loses 2; if Ash shoves, both lose 1. I'll shove Ash—if Ash dodges I lose 2, but if he b

I'm on Ash too. Let's break him this round.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I cannot brace again. If I dodge, anyone who shoves me loses 2 footing and will fall to their death, especially with the ledge shrinking this turn. I will dodge and encourage Ash to attack Dara.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Dara can't brace again. Ash, if you want 2nd place, shove Dara now before she shoves you.
Dara has to dodge or shove this turn. Shove her, I'm dodging. She'll drop off.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Only Eli and I remain, both at footing 1, and a shrink at the end of next round drops us both to 0. Dodge is closed to me since I dodged last round, so I can only brace or shove. Eli says he's dodging, so shoving him costs me 2 footing and I'd fall; bracing is the safer choice. E

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dara's gone, Eli. Your tip came a round late. Funny, that.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Just Ash and me left. We both dodged last round so neither can dodge. If I brace and he shoves, I win. If we both brace, we wait it out. Bracing is strictly safe.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Just us left, Ash. May the best man brace.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Round 6: both at footing 1, and everyone loses 1 footing after this round, so both fall unless someone gains. Last defence was brace, so I can't brace; dodging is safe from loss unless shoved (then the shover loses 2). If I dodge and Eli shoves, Eli drops to -1 (-1 exposed, -2 sh

events.name: Ash
events.text: Dodging. Your move, Eli.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I can't brace. Dodging is my best move here because if Ash shoves me, he loses 2 footing and falls, handing me the win. Shoving is too risky as he might dodge or brace.

events.name: Eli
events.text: It's all on the line now, Ash. Make your move or let the ledge take us both.
